source_text:
3.17 Ἀφρικανοῦ· περὶ
συκῶν καὶ μυρμηκιῶν καὶ ἀκροχορδόνων Μυρμηκίαι εἰσὶν σωμάτων ἐκφύσεις
τραχέσιν ἥλοις προσεοικυῖαι· γίνονται δὲ πολλοῖς πολλαχοῦ. «Μυρμηκίας» δὲ
καλοῦσιν τὸ πάθος, ἃ πολλοὶ δεισιδαίμονες καὶ σημεῖά τινος αὐτοῖς συμβησομένου
τίθενται. Ὧν ἡ ἀπαλλαγὴ ποικίλη καὶ πᾶσι πεπειραμένη. Οἱ μὲν γὰρ ἐπιφυλάξαντες
οὐρήσαντα <κύνα> κατὰ γῆς τὸν πηλὸν ἀναφυράσαντες ἐπέθηκαν τῷ τόπῳ καὶ τὸ
αἴτιον τῷ πηλῷ συναπέκλεισαν· ἄλλοι δ' ἐλατήριον τρίψαντες καὶ ἐπιτιθέντες οὕτω
περιεγένοντο· ἢ κιχορίου ἄνθος, ὅπερ κυρίως «ἡλιοτρόπιον» καλεῖται, πρὸ ἀνατολῆς
ἡλίου ἀφελόντες <...> τρὶς περίγραφε τὸν τόπον καὶ ἡ μυρμηκία παύσεται.
pass_a_gloss: 3.17 Of-Africanus: about figs and myrmekiai and acrochordonas. Myrmekiai are of-bodies outgrowths to-rough nails resembling; they-become but to-many in-many-places. 'Myrmekias' but they-call the affection, which many superstitious also signs of-some to-them about-to-happen they-set. Of-which the riddance various and by-all having-been-tried. Some for having-watched a-dog having-urined according-to earth the mud having-kneaded-up they-set-on to-the-place and the cause with-the-mud they-shut-together; others but elaterion having-rubbed and setting-on thus they-prevailed; or of-chicory a-flower, which properly 'heliotrope' is-called, before rising of-sun having-taken [lacuna] thrice draw-round the place and the myrmekia will-cease.
pass_b_english: Of Africanus: about figs and myrmekiai and acrochordonas. Myrmekiai are outgrowths of bodies resembling rough nails; they come to be for many in many places. They call the affection myrmekiai, which many superstitious people also set as signs of something about to happen to them. The riddance of them is various and tried by all.

Some, having watched a dog urinate on the ground, kneaded up the mud, set it on the place, and shut the cause together with the mud. Others, having rubbed elaterion and setting it on, thus prevailed. Or the flower of chicory, which is properly called heliotrope: having taken it before the rising of the sun [lacuna], draw round the place three times and the myrmekia will cease.

choices.why: Kept as the lock's disease-name (ant-like warts), not flattened to 'warts' which the lock also has as ἀκροχορδόνες.

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
